summary: Contestants will develop a mobile application titled SafelyGo to promote student safety on and around campus. The app must include features such as safety reporting, emergency contacts, location sharing, a live campus safety map, user registration, account recovery, an admin panel, database integration, and at least one API. Submissions are made virtually and include a URL, written description, source code, screenshots, works cited, release forms, and AI documentation.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes for setup
No more than ten (10) minutes for the presentation
No more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
submission_requirements: Submit one combined PDF file containing the mobile application, written description of the project and details of a design concept, source code, application screenshots, Works Cited formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual, BPA Release Form(s), and the AI Usage and Documentation Form
Contestant ID is required for all submissions
Materials must follow the organization’s BPA Graphic Standards and make proper use of the BPA logo and/or organization’s name
presubmit_items: A clickable URL to the mobile application
Written description of the project and details of a design concept
deadlines: Event registration deadline is no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, on December 1, 2026
National Deadline: January 15, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
competencies: Implement system analysis and design concepts to plan, structure, and guide the architecture of a mobile application
Develop a comprehensive project plan and timeline to manage all phases of the mobile application development lifecycle
Demonstrate knowledge of program implementation, testing, and deployment processes, including strategies for identifying and resolving technical issues
Apply Google Android® or Apple iOS® platform-specific programming languages, tools, and techniques to develop a functional mobile application

Demonstrate proficiency in core programming language concepts — including object-oriented, structured, and procedural techniques — applying variables, assignment statements, mathematical operators, decision-making controls, and iterative structures to implement application logic

Design a graphical user interface (GUI) for a mobile device by applying design and color principles, incorporating user input controls, icons, images, and other graphic elements to create an intuitive and visually consistent user experience

Employ database skills and applied programming techniques — including data management, sequential file access, I/O operations, and internal and external function and/or procedure calls — to handle and persist in application data
Integrate external Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) to extend application functionality and connect to third-party data sources and services
Apply internal programming documentation standards to ensure code clarity, maintainability, and long-term readability

eligibility_notes: Any middle level, secondary or postsecondary contestant may enter this event.
There are no restrictions on the number of entries per chapter or per state.

Contestants who do not submit an entry following the topic listed below or do not follow the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation policy will be disqualified.
Contestant ID is required for all submissions. Materials from non-registered contestants and/or those missing Contestant ID cannot be accepted.
